description: Roman fort and associated vicus, the fort is dated from 75 CE - between 120 and 160 CE, the vicus continued until the early 3rd CE. Investigations revealed an un-enclosed area with evidence for burning that led to the suggestion of a shrine.
bibliography: Hopewell, and Burman. “Geophysical Survey at Caer Gai and Cefn Caer Roman Forts.” Archaeology in Wales 47 (2007).
Martyn, Blick, Brindle, and et al. “Caer Gai, Llanwchlyn (Gwynedd).” The Rural Settlement of Roman Britain: an online resource, 2015. https://doi.org/10.5284/1030449.
